questions.corrige_markdown:
Multiply every entry of $A$ by $2$: $2A=\begin{pmatrix}4&-8\\6&12\end{pmatrix}$.

Add the entries in the same positions:

$2A+B=\begin{pmatrix}4+(-3)&-8+8\\6+(-6)&12+(-11)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$.

**Answer: $2A+B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: b) Write down the name of the resulting matrix $2A+B$. *[5 marks for the whole question]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A square matrix with $1$ on the leading diagonal and $0$ everywhere else is called the identity matrix (unit matrix) of order $2\times2$, written $I$. Multiplying any $2\times2$ matrix by it leaves that matrix unchanged.

**Answer: the identity matrix (unit matrix) $I$.**
